names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 26 iunie, «Sfântul Ierarh Ioan, Episcopul Goției»; the form is the bare name, the rest of the line being rank and see.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Ιωάννης επίσκοπος Γοτθίας», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 19. мај ст. ст., „Свети Јован епископ готски.“ — Свети is not a rank and „епископ готски“ is the rank and the see, which this corpus puts in `types` as `bishop` and in `office` as Bishop; **stripping a rank and a see to reach the stored form is the reading BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §6 asks be said in the note**, and here it leaves a bare forename with nothing beside it — Georgia, Bessarabia, the kagan and the century are all in the body. **«Јован Готски» is nowhere on the page** and a form a reader builds is what §6 forbids. **So this is a deliberate ninth joining of the bare «Јован»**: `foldchk.py` returned eight holders before a line was drafted, every one of them an `sr` form from this same book on another Julian day, and the fold is read in this batch’s commit message.

The nominative the day page's own `/name/971.html` link carries in its `title`, «Святитель Иоанн Готфский, епископ», with «Святитель» and the trailing «епископ» left off — the latter is the `bishop` this folder carries in `types`, with the see in `office`. The day's own line ranks him «Прп.», venerable, where the name link makes him a hierarch; the `types` were left as they stood and the line's rank word was not written. `fk.mjs` on «Иоанн Готфский» returned NONE before the write, in a corpus holding over a hundred folders of the bare forename.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru, 19 мая ст. ст.: the day line prints «Прп. Иоанна , еп. Готфского (790)» and the life page says «через 40 дней святитель скончался, это произошло в то время, когда он обращался с поучением к народу, в 790 году». The year falls inside the interval this folder carried before, which is kept here whole: that reading was «8th century», read off the page that made the folder, which said only that he lived in the eighth century and gave no year at all. The same Russian page dates the iconoclast emperor Constantine Copronymus 741 to 775 and has him driven out of the see in that reign, which 790 does not contradict.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 мая ст. ст. — «Прп. Иоанна , еп. Готфского (790).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the folder already keeps, and the same man. **`dates` were REPLACED by the year inside the century they held**, on the `pausikakos-of-synada` precedent: the folder carried «8th century» and nothing else, the day line prints «(790)» and the page says «через 40 дней святитель скончался, это произошло ... в 790 году», which falls inside the century it replaces and is also consistent with the reign of Constantine Copronymus the same page dates 741–775. The old reading is carried forward whole in the new note. The page's own «Дни памяти» line adds «26 июня», which the calendar does not explain and which the day page for 19 мая does not repeat; one row per church is the schema, so it is recorded here and he does not render on it. The day page prints no hymn for him. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 iunie — «Sfântul Ierarh Ioan, Episcopul Goției»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης επίσκοπος Γοτθίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the see and the iconoclasm settle the identity: a bishop of Gothia in the eighth century who died in exile. Its heading reads «Οσιος Ιωαννης Επισκοπος Γοτθιας (; - 780)», and the narrative adds the parents' names, Leo and Photine, the reign of Leo the Isaurian, the flight to Amastris and the year 780 — none of which the folder's Romanian source gives, which is why no `dates` object is proposed. The Romanian life has his consecration from the bishop of Iberia; the Greek page says only that in the years of the iconoclasm he kept church communion rather with Rome. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.06.2026 (19. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети Јован епископ готски.“

attestations.note: **The day list could not see this folder**, because the Romanian and Greek rows keep him on the menologion **26/6** and the Prologue keeps him on the **19/5**; the list matches on the menologion number and offered fifty-seven folders without this one. He was found by `ls saints | grep -iE 'goth'`, which is the fourth day in five that a hand grep has caught what the list could not. **The identification is not in doubt** — a bishop of Gothia, a Tatar persecution, four years away among the Goths, the eighth century — but **this book disagrees with the other two at three points and agrees with them at one, and none of the three disagreements is resolved here.** (1) „Би епископ у Грузији“ makes him **bishop in Georgia**, where doxologia has him only **sent to the bishop of Iberia, that is of Georgia, to be consecrated**, his own see being Gothia. (2) The four years away are spent **„међу Готе у Бесарабију“**, among the Goths in Bessarabia, where saint.gr has him take refuge **at Amastris on the Black Sea** — and **the four years themselves match exactly**, which is the agreement and is the strongest reason to think it one event told twice. (3) This book has him **hear of the kagan’s death, return to his service and guide his flock zealously, and fall asleep in peace**, where doxologia has him **pass to the Lord at Amastris in Pontus** and saint.gr has him **die there in 780**. **A FIRST DATE FOR A FOLDER THAT HELD NO `dates` OBJECT**: „Упокоји се мирно у VIII веку“ → `death` 701–800, „8th century“. **saint.gr’s 780 falls inside it and is the narrower reading, and it is not written**: it stands in this folder’s life already, an earlier reader recorded it and did not write it, and this reader writes only what his own source states. **Narrowing the century to 780 is the author’s, in one commit**, and `date-citation-audit.mjs` is the instrument that will keep asking for it. **New here**: the parenthesis **„(Готска епархија образована за време Константина Великог)“**, that the Gothic diocese was formed in the time of Constantine the Great, which no other book read for him says; that the persecutor was **„каган татарски“**, a Tatar kagan, where doxologia has only „some bloody rising“ and the nobles of the Lazi; and **the prophecy of his own death** — „Кроз четрдесет дана одлазим да се судим са каганом“, in forty days I go to be judged with the kagan, which the Prologue glosses itself as going through death before the throne of God — **and that on the fortieth day he departed**. `types` untouched: Свети is no rank and „епископ готски“ is the `bishop` and the `office` the folder already holds, and the `confessor` it carries is the iconoclast years, which this entry does not mention. **Constantine the Great takes no row**: a diocese founded in his reign is not a relation, by the same rule that makes a dedication none. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
